pages.quiz:
SOCIAL STUDIES — MOCK EXAM #5
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. On a map, the market is drawn above the school. Which direction is the market from the school? (1 mark)
   A. East
   B. West
   C. North
   D. South

2. A pupil faces the rising sun in the morning. Which direction is on the pupil's left hand? (1 mark)
   A. East
   B. North
   C. West
   D. South

3. Which county contains the capital city of Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Kisumu
   B. Nakuru
   C. Nairobi
   D. Kitui

4. Which of these counties has a coast on the Indian Ocean? (1 mark)
   A. Kilifi
   B. Nakuru
   C. Nyeri
   D. Kitui

5. A county is divided into smaller parts called what? (1 mark)
   A. Sub-counties
   B. Oceans
   C. Countries
   D. Continents

6. Which physical feature helps people to catch fish? (1 mark)
   A. A plateau
   B. A hill
   C. A lake
   D. A plain

7. In many parts of Kenya, when do the long rains usually come? (1 mark)
   A. June to August
   B. January to February
   C. September only
   D. March to May

8. Which of these is a problem of the rainy season? (1 mark)
   A. Shortage of rain
   B. Flooding and muddy roads
   C. Very dry grass
   D. Thick dust

9. Which of these is most likely to happen in the rainy season? (1 mark)
   A. Grass dries up completely
   B. Herders move very far for water
   C. Farmers harvest all their maize
   D. Rivers fill with water

10. Which of these is one of the four seasons in the county? (1 mark)
   A. Winter
   B. Autumn
   C. Spring
   D. Rainy season

11. What does UNESCO do for important old places? (1 mark)
   A. Paints them
   B. Helps to protect them
   C. Moves them to other countries
   D. Sells them

12. Fort Jesus is found in which town? (1 mark)
   A. Kisumu
   B. Nakuru
   C. Eldoret
   D. Mombasa

13. How is money useful in trade? (1 mark)
   A. It stops trade
   B. It grows crops
   C. It builds houses
   D. It makes buying and selling easier

14. Which place is used mainly for prayers and worship? (1 mark)
   A. Hospital
   B. Church, mosque or temple
   C. Factory
   D. Market

15. On a dot map, what does a group of many dots close together show? (1 mark)
   A. A crowded area
   B. A river
   C. An empty area
   D. A road

16. Which of these counties has a very dense city population? (1 mark)
   A. Marsabit
   B. Nairobi
   C. Wajir
   D. Turkana

17. What does respect mean? (1 mark)
   A. Breaking things
   B. Insulting people
   C. Treating people and things with honour
   D. Ignoring people

18. Which national park in Narok County is famous for wildlife? (1 mark)
   A. Nakuru town
   B. Kakamega
   C. Maasai Mara
   D. Lake Victoria

19. Reduce, reuse and recycle are ways of doing what? (1 mark)
   A. Cutting down waste
   B. Growing tea
   C. Building roads
   D. Drying fish

20. Which industry uses milk as raw material? (1 mark)
   A. A shoe workshop
   B. A sugar mill
   C. A cement plant
   D. A dairy

21. In Figure 3 of the lesson, the sugar factory employs 7 hundred workers. How many workers is that? (1 mark)
   A. 7,000
   B. 70
   C. 700
   D. 7

22. Wanjiru sold 10 tomatoes but recorded only 8. What should she do? (1 mark)
   A. Hide the money
   B. Correct the record and tell the treasurer
   C. Keep quiet
   D. Blame a friend

23. What is a project? (1 mark)
   A. A type of shoe
   B. A holiday
   C. A plan of work with a start, a finish and a goal
   D. A kind of fruit

24. Why should every sale be recorded? (1 mark)
   A. So that profit disappears
   B. So that pupils have more homework
   C. So that the project fails
   D. So that money can be checked and accounted for

25. What is the Kiswahili word for peace? (1 mark)
   A. Amani
   B. Shule
   C. Chakula
   D. Rafiki

26. Which item usually comes last on an agenda? (1 mark)
   A. Reports
   B. Closing remarks
   C. Opening prayer
   D. Reading of minutes

27. How can you show respect for community leaders? (1 mark)
   A. Spread rumours
   B. Listen politely and follow fair rules
   C. Insult them
   D. Refuse to attend meetings

28. How often are governors elected? (1 mark)
   A. Every five years
   B. Every year
   C. Every twenty years
   D. Every month

29. What are ECDE and pre-primary schools run by? (1 mark)
   A. Private banks only
   B. The army
   C. Foreign governments
   D. County governments

30. What does MCA stand for? (1 mark)
   A. Minister of County Administration
   B. Master of County Affairs
   C. Member of the County Assembly
   D. Mayor of Central Area

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. State three causes of child abuse in a community. (3 marks)

32. Describe how to interview an elder about traditional culture politely. (4 marks)

33. A pupil stands facing east. Say what is behind the pupil, on the left and on the right. (3 marks)

34. Give four school rules and one reason for each. (4 marks)

35. Design a poster: write a slogan and list three qualities of a good leader you would show on it. (5 marks)

36. State three benefits of interdependence in a county. (3 marks)

37. Give three rules for using safe school transport. (3 marks)

38. State three qualities of a good citizen in school and give an example for each. (3 marks)

39. Give two responsibilities of a child at school. (2 marks)

40. Give three ways in which the dry season affects people's activities. (3 marks)

41. Explain why the county assembly must check the work of the governor. (5 marks)

42. Explain why traditional culture is important. (3 marks)

43. List four rules that visitors should follow at a historic place. (4 marks)

44. Give three school values and say why each is important. (3 marks)

45. Explain why a monument is built. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — MOCK EXAM #5 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — North
   Above means north when north is at the top.

2. B — North
   Facing east, north is on the left and south is on the right.

3. C — Nairobi
   Nairobi County contains Kenya's capital city.

4. A — Kilifi
   Kilifi lies along the coast.

5. A — Sub-counties
   Counties are divided into sub-counties, and sub-counties into wards.

6. C — A lake
   People fish in lakes, rivers and the ocean.

7. D — March to May
   The long rains are usually from March to May.

8. B — Flooding and muddy roads
   Heavy rain can flood rivers and make roads muddy.

9. D — Rivers fill with water
   Rain fills rivers and streams.

10. D — Rainy season
   The four seasons are hot, cold, dry and rainy.

11. B — Helps to protect them
   UNESCO names World Heritage Sites and helps to protect them.

12. D — Mombasa
   Fort Jesus is a fort at Mombasa.

13. D — It makes buying and selling easier
   Money is a common way of paying for goods and services.

14. B — Church, mosque or temple
   Places of worship are for prayer.

15. A — A crowded area
   Many dots show many people.

16. B — Nairobi
   Nairobi has a large city population.

17. C — Treating people and things with honour
   Respect is showing care and honour.

18. C — Maasai Mara
   The Maasai Mara is in Narok County.

19. A — Cutting down waste
   The three Rs cut down waste.

20. D — A dairy
   Dairies process milk.

21. C — 700
   7 hundreds = 700.

22. B — Correct the record and tell the treasurer
   Records must be honest and complete.

23. C — A plan of work with a start, a finish and a goal
   A project is planned work for a goal.

24. D — So that money can be checked and accounted for
   Records show that money was handled honestly.

25. A — Amani
   Amani means peace.

26. B — Closing remarks
   Meetings end with closing remarks.

27. B — Listen politely and follow fair rules
   Respect means polite listening and obeying good rules.

28. A — Every five years
   General elections are held every five years.

29. D — County governments
   Pre-primary education is a county function.

30. C — Member of the County Assembly
   MCA is a Member of the County Assembly.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: Poverty, harmful beliefs and lack of knowledge of the law. Accept greed or conflict.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each cause.

32. (4 marks)
   Answer: Greet the elder respectfully, ask permission before recording or taking photographs, listen without interrupting, and say thank you.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct step.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: Behind is west. On the left is north. On the right is south.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct direction.

34. (4 marks)
   Answer: Come on time to avoid missing lessons; keep the school clean for health; respect others for peace; care for property so it lasts.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule with a reason.

35. (5 marks)
   Answer: A slogan such as A Good Leader Serves, and qualities such as honest, fair and kind, with a picture.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a slogan, 3 marks for three qualities, 1 mark for a picture.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: People get goods and services they cannot make, people help each other in trouble, and the county develops faster.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each benefit.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: Use only transport approved by the school and parents, do not take lifts from strangers, and do not board overloaded vehicles.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: Honesty: returning lost items. Respect: greeting teachers. Responsibility: doing class duties.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each quality with example.

39. (2 marks)
   Answer: Attend and study hard, and respect others. Accept care for property.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each responsibility.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: Farmers harvest and dry crops, fishermen dry fish in the sun, and herders move animals to find water and grass.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

41. (5 marks)
   Answer: To make sure county money is used honestly, to prevent misuse of power, to make sure services reach people, to protect citizens' interests, and to keep the governor accountable.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid reason.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: It gives identity, teaches values, and brings people together.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: Do not litter, do not write on walls, do not climb or touch old structures, and listen to the guide.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct rule.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Honesty helps us to be trusted. Respect keeps peace. Responsibility helps us to do our duties. Accept other valid values.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each value with a reason.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: A monument is built to remind people of an important person or event so that they remember it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for reminding people, 1 mark for the idea of a person or event.
